claims.text: Integrating disorder-sensitive machine learning with atomistic modeling will improve forecasts of low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
Explicitly accounting for compositional randomness will improve prediction accuracy because compositional randomness affects phonon scattering.
The target materials are compositionally disordered, single-phase high-entropy alloys with simple BCC or FCC structures.
The predictive model will use disorder metrics together with conventional structural descriptors as input features.
Compositional disorder increases phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Traditional predictive methods do not fully capture disorder-induced phonon scattering.
Local variations in atomic masses and bonding characterize the degree and type of disorder relevant to phonon transport.
Training on computational and experimental data will allow the model to identify features associated with enhanced phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
A disorder-sensitive model will be more sensitive to relevant transport features than models based on averaged structural parameters.
The proposed approach will reduce prediction RMSE by approximately 10–20% relative to conventional predictive methods.
The approach is expected to apply mainly to simple BCC or FCC high-entropy alloys with moderate atomic-size mismatch.
The approach may be unreliable for extreme atomic-size mismatches or multiphase materials in which additional scattering mechanisms dominate.
Prediction improvement will depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
Failure to achieve at least a 10% RMSE reduction against conventional methods within the stated applicability domain will falsify the hypothesis.
